topic: A person's invention is already patented by someone else
text: Master, the news from the town brings a shadow that darkens the fields and my heart. It’s said another has claimed the very craft I’ve toiled over, like someone planting their flag on the land you’ve tended since you were but a lad. The words of the law, I’ve been told, now protect this other’s seed, though it sprouted from the same soil as mine. The days grow short, and the frost nips at the edges of my thoughts. I’ve poured my sweat into the earth, and now, it seems, the harvest may slip through my fingers. The thoughts of what to do next weigh heavy, heavier than any scythe I’ve wielded. What shall become of the season’s work, if not to be reaped by my own hands?
